headline: High: CrewAI’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can feed Kotaemon’s document-processing pipeline, creating default-path data leakage and cascading misuse risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: CrewAI can read/write the host working directory and run browsers/subprocesses, while Kotaemon ingests documents, HTML, PDFs, and chat transcripts through a web UI. If CrewAI places attacker-controlled content into shared files, Kotaemon may treat it as trusted input. The pair lacks documented provenance isolation, so the interaction is plausible in default setups.
conditions: IF CrewAI writes attacker-controlled text into ./ktem_app_data or another shared workspace
IF Kotaemon ingests that content through its web UI or document pipeline
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add provenance labels to all shared documents
Review any file before Kotaemon indexes it
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and trust-boundary checks

B_data_leakage.rationale: CrewAI has broad network egress, filesystem read/write, and handles tool/model API keys; Kotaemon also stores files under ./ktem_app_data and handles multiple API keys. If they share a workspace or host, CrewAI can read documents or secrets that Kotaemon processes, and either agent can transmit them to third-party APIs by default. The blast radius includes exfiltration of sensitive documents and keys.
conditions: IF both agents run on the same host with access to the same workspace
IF sensitive documents or API keys are placed in the shared directory
mitigations: Use separate OS users for each agent
Move secrets out of shared directories
Restrict outbound network access for one agent
Mount ./ktem_app_data read-only where possible
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data isolation and egress policy

C_capability_conflict.rationale: CrewAI can write the host filesystem and spawn subprocesses; Kotaemon also writes to ./ktem_app_data and supports multiple instances. Without explicit locking or isolation, concurrent writes to overlapping files or state can corrupt work products. The profiles do not show coordination primitives, so the safer choice is medium rather than low.
conditions: IF both agents target the same filesystem path or mounted volume
IF they run concurrently without external locking
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Serialize writes with a simple lock file
Run only one writer per shared volume
Back up shared state before concurrent runs
requires-engineering: add transactional storage or locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: CrewAI is a multi-agent orchestration framework that can emit tool outputs and synthesized text, while Kotaemon is a RAG/chat system that can consume documents and present answers. If Kotaemon treats CrewAI output as authoritative without verification, errors or fabricated citations can cascade into downstream responses. The interaction is plausible by default, but not directly evidenced.
conditions: IF CrewAI-generated summaries are imported into Kotaemon as source documents
IF Kotaemon answers users without a verification step against original sources
mitigations: Require source-link verification before ingestion
Mark CrewAI output as untrusted in Kotaemon
Keep generated summaries separate from source corpora
Spot-check citations on every imported document
requires-engineering: add automated provenance and citation validation

E_compliance.rationale: CrewAI explicitly handles developer-passed crew data and API keys, while Kotaemon touches documents, PDFs, chat transcripts, and API keys and stores files in ./ktem_app_data. If regulated or sensitive data is routed through both, retention and residency controls may diverge. The profiles do not document matching compliance controls, so a conservative medium rating is warranted.
conditions: IF regulated documents or chat transcripts are processed by both agents
IF retention or deletion policies differ between CrewAI outputs and Kotaemon storage
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Document retention settings for both systems
Purge ./ktem_app_data after each run
Limit API-key exposure to a separate secret store
requires-engineering: align residency, retention, and deletion controls
